feature2.name: feature_benefits
feature2.label: Why It's Fair
feature2.title: A Draw Your League Can't Argue With
feature2.description: Fairness here is engineering, not a promise — every property below is how the tool actually works.

items.title: Crypto-grade randomness
items.description: Every random NFL team draw uses your browser's crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling — no modulo bias, no favorite clubs, no pattern for anyone to game.

items.title: No duplicate deals
items.description: Assigning 32 people yields all 32 clubs exactly once. The engine shuffles once and deals from the top — it never draws with replacement.

items.title: Instant, in your browser
items.description: No server round-trip, no waiting on a spinner. The draw runs locally and completes before you could blink at a slower tool.

items.title: Copy-ready audit trail
items.description: Every result copies as plain text with the mode and pool attached — a record the group can check, keep, and replay.

items.title: Free, no account
items.description: No sign-up, no paywall after three draws, no email harvest. Open the page, draw, leave.

items.title: Verified 32-club list
items.description: The dataset holds the 32 current NFL clubs with correct conferences and divisions, checked against nfl.com/teams before each season.

items.title: Is the draw actually random and fair?
items.description: Yes. Every draw runs a Fisher-Yates shuffle seeded by your browser's crypto.getRandomValues, with rejection sampling to remove modulo bias. Each club in the pool has exactly the same chance of landing in any slot, and the whole draw happens locally on your device.

items.title: How do I assign NFL teams for a fantasy football league?
items.description: Switch to 'Assign to people', paste your league members one per line, then draw. Each participant is dealt a different club — a 32-person league uses all 32 teams exactly once. Copy the result into your group chat as the record of the draw.

items.title: Can I randomize by conference or division?
items.description: Yes. The Pool dropdown narrows the draw to the AFC, the NFC, or any single division (4 clubs). The counter beside it always shows how many clubs are currently eligible, so a division-only deal tops out at 4 people.

items.title: How many teams can I pick at once?
items.description: Any number from 1 up to the pool size (32 for the whole league). Random NFL team picks are drawn without duplicates — for a complete ranked order of every team, use Shuffle mode instead.

items.title: Can I use this as a random NFL team wheel?
items.description: The single-team pick does the same job as a spinning wheel — one fair, random club with a visible result — just without the spin animation. If you need the theater of a wheel for a party, draw in Shuffle mode and reveal the list one line at a time.

items.title: Is the team list up to date?
items.description: The dataset contains the 32 current NFL clubs with their correct conferences and divisions, verified against nfl.com/teams ahead of the 2026 season and reviewed every preseason. Club names and locations follow their current official usage.

items.title: Is this tool affiliated with the NFL?
items.description: No. This is an unofficial, fan-made utility. NFL team names and marks are trademarks of the NFL and its member clubs; this site is not affiliated with, sponsored, or endorsed by the NFL in any way.

items.title: Is it free to use?
items.description: Completely free, with no account, no sign-up wall, and no limit on how often you draw. The tool runs entirely in your browser, so you can reroll as many times as the league demands.
